what: Minor point. LONG_LIST_REPLAY is described as 'one exported constant', but the acceptance test at line 266 sets it to 'worker' inside the test. An ES module constant cannot be reassigned from a test. The instruction does not say how the test should switch it, for example with vi.mock, an injectable option, or a setter used only by tests. Without that, the agent has to guess, and both readings may not get tested on the same build.

Gap 1 is mostly closed: the long-list design is cited at line 41, attack 28 builds the 2500-move and 20000-move links with a late forbidden move, line 139 switches the unit check away from bad(), and method F names firstForbiddenMove. The revision describes only the proposed worker design, though, and never says that the P1-A2 instruction (section 5.3, line 129; acceptance line 265; trap 12) makes the contract reading the default. Under that reading LONG_LIST_REPLAY is 'sync' and gate G1 tests it: decodeState replays every list of up to 20000 moves itself, on the main thread, and returns the defaults and the notice. Attack 28 contradicts that default in two places. It says 'the worker must have been requested, whichever reading MERGE chose', yet under 'sync' the forbidden link fails inside decodeState and no worker call is needed. It also lists 'the replay run on the main thread for more than 2000 moves' as a failure, yet that is exactly what the default reading does by design, and P1-A2 records it as a deviation for MERGE to decide. If MERGE keeps the default, an attacker following attack 28 would report the planned behaviour as findings. The attack should name the switch LONG_LIST_REPLAY and its 'sync' default, and should make the worker-request and main-thread failure conditions apply only under the 'worker' reading. Under 'sync', the main-thread replay should be reported as a note against E-9 rule 2 that cites the open deviation.
